title: US DOJ Indicts Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya + 9 Officials for Chapitos Drug Conspiracy — First Sitting Mexican Governor Charged in US History
detail: The US Department of Justice (Southern District of New York) unsealed a 34-page federal indictment on April 29–30, 2026 charging Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other current or former Mexican officials with drug trafficking conspiracy, weapons charges, and conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices — all on behalf of Los Chapitos. It marks the first time a sitting Mexican state governor has been federally indicted in US history. The full defendant list: (1) Gov. Rubén Rocha Moya — alleged to have facilitated cartel election interference including ballot-box theft, kidnapping of opposition candidates, and intimidation of rivals before the 2021 election, in exchange for placing cartel-friendly officials across state government; (2) Juan de Dios Gámez Mendívil, Mayor of Culiacán — allegedly ordered Municipal Police to escort Chapitos drug shipments to the US border, receiving ~300,000 MXN/month (~$15,000 USD); (3) Enrique Inzunza Cazárez, Morena state senator; (4) Enrique Díaz Vega, former Secretary of Administration and Finance; (5) Dámaso Castro Zaavedra, Vice-Fiscal General — allegedly protected cartel members from prosecution and reported law enforcement operations to the cartel (~200,000 MXN/month); (6) Gerardo Mérida Sánchez, former Secretary of Public Security — warned Chapitos at least 10 times in advance of raids on drug labs, allowing personnel and materials to escape (~$100,000 USD/month — the highest individual bribe); (7) Marco Antonio Almanzas Avilés, former chief of the State Investigative Police — issued arrest warrants against Chapitos rivals and released detained Chapitos members (300,000 MXN/month shared); (8) Alberto Jorge Contreras Núñez ('Cholo'), former co-chief of State Investigative Police (300,000 MXN/month shared); (9) José Antonio Dionisio Hipólito ('Tornado'), former Sub-Director State Police (~100,000 MXN/month); (10) Juan Valenzuela Millán ('Juanito'), former Culiacán Municipal Police commander — faces mandatory life sentence for alleged involvement in kidnappings of a DEA source and a family member that resulted in deaths. The protected trafficking network funneled fentanyl, heroin, cocaine, and methamphetamine through Arizona as the primary US distribution hub. Governor Rocha Moya denied the charges via social media as 'a perverse strategy to violate the constitutional order.' Mayor Gámez Mendívil also denied all allegations. The indictment was coordinated with OFAC's April 24 sanctions on a 23-person fentanyl precursor network and the State Department's April 20 visa restrictions on 75 Sinaloa Cartel associates — representing the culmination of a sustained week of maximum US pressure on the Chapitos political-criminal network in Sinaloa.
